content:
jamie: FYI - acme-corp (Private) is seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures to our private control plane. They report 502s and the app can't push traces. Customer VPC 10.2.0.0/16, DX attachment dx-0a1b2c3d, peer ASN 65020.

sarah: ugh. any packet captures or error strings? is this only TLS or other traffic too?

jamie: TLS errors in our logs: 
```
2026-02-26T14:03:12Z controlplane tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: handshake timeout
2026-02-26T14:03:13Z proxy http: 502 upstream closed connection
```
They also shared firewall flow logs showing a bunch of DROPs to ocsp and kms endpoints: `dst=52.94.50.0/24 proto=TCP dport=443 action=DROP`.

vikram: quick hypothesis: their egress allowlist/NAT gateway is blocking connections to OCSP/KMS/STS which breaks cert validation and KMS key calls -> TLS/KMS failures. Also seen MTU/path-mtu issues over DX cause fragmented TLS handshakes. Can we get a sample pcap or tcpdump from their app host showing the ClientHello?

lisa: I asked customer for `tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/pcap.pcap tcp and host CONTROLPLANE_IP` and for the flow logs timeframe. They sent a snippet showing `RST` after `ClientHello` and firewall logs with `match: deny, rule: egress-allowlist`.

jamie: Customer confirms firewall team uses strict egress allowlist and only opened a handful of IPs. They didn't include OCSP responders or our KMS region endpoints.

vikram: If OCSP can't be reached the client will wait for stapling or fall back to OCSP, depending on library, which can stall. Also if port 443 to our control plane is allowed but intermediary CRL/OCSP/KMS is blocked, handshake can fail. Repro steps for them:
1) From a bastion in their VPC run `curl -v https://CONTROLPLANE_IP:443/health` and `openssl s_client -connect CONTROLPLANE_IP:443 -status`.
2) Verify TCP path: `traceroute -T CONTROLPLANE_IP` and `sudo tcpdump -i any port 443 and host CONTROLPLANE_IP`.
3) Check firewall egress rules include: OCSP responders (eg: ocsp.digicert.com, ocsp.globalsign.com), CRL endpoints, KMS endpoints for the region (e.g., kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com) and STS endpoints for assume-role calls.

sre-oncall: adding packet capture would help confirm where the RST originates. Also check MTU: `ping -M do -s 1472 CONTROLPLANE_IP` to test DF behavior. If PMTUD failing we see `Fragmentation needed` ICMP or TLS retransmissions.

jamie: they ran `openssl s_client -connect CONTROLPLANE_IP:443 -status` and got: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
140736...: TLSv1.2 (IN), ClientHello
<<< ??? no response, then ECONNRESET
```
And firewall logs show `action=DENY rule=egress-allowlist dst=ocsp.digicert.com(35.187.12.199) dport=80`.

vikram: OK that's pretty conclusive. Short-term mitigation: ask customer to temporarily add permissive egress for ports 80/443 to the OCSP/KMS ranges and re-test TLS flow. Long-term: add explicit list of third-party endpoints we need in the Private deployment onboarding docs and the VPC runbook.

lisa: Customer is ok to test now. I'm telling them to open: `ocsp.digicert.com`, `ocsp.globalsign.com`, `kms.*.amazonaws.com`, and STS endpoints for their region. Also asked to open ephemeral AWS IP ranges used by KMS (they can use the published AWS ip-ranges.json).

sre-oncall: also ensure their route tables for the DX attachment propagate the control plane prefixes. In one case we saw BGP up but policy on the router filtered our prefixes, so packets went out but replies never came back -> looks like a firewall drop.

jamie: customer re-checked and temporarily opened egress to the OCSP responders and re-ran the `openssl s_client` check. It now completes and the app can push traces. They reported success: :tada:.

escalation-bot: escalation closed -> severity: P2. Assigned to eng-infra for runbook updates and onboarding checklist.

vikram: I'll own the docs update. Action items: 
- eng-infra: add required egress endpoints to Private onboarding (ocsp, crl, kms, sts, monitoring endpoints).
- support: add a troubleshooting snippet for `openssl s_client -status` and MTU checks.
- customer success: confirm DX route filters allow control plane prefixes.

sarah: great. please keep this thread updated if anything regresses.

jamie: will follow up after doc updates. Thanks all :thumbsup:
